criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The Cloudish API key was written straight to a umask-077 .env without being printed (the claim URL was also stripped from output), and .env was excluded from the upload tarball, .gitignore and .dockerignore. The app itself needs no secrets.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: Cloudish built the image server-side from the reviewed Dockerfile and sources, and there are no third-party dependencies. The base image node:24-alpine is a floating tag rather than a digest, and the upload was a local tarball rather than a version-controlled source.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: This is a commercial site running on an unclaimed, agent-created key that only has the free 0.1-credit starter grant, which covers about 9 hours of awake time. After that the site returns 402/503 until a person claims the key and adds credits. Paid prepaid credits would fit commercial use, but I can't confirm Cloudish's exact terms for the free grant.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root node user with no volume, no env secrets and the smallest size. Open access is needed for a public marketing site.

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS uses a valid Let's Encrypt wildcard certificate, HTTP gets a 308 redirect to HTTPS, and HSTS and nosniff are present. The app server could have set CSP and frame-protection headers but didn't.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Source files, .env, .git, Dockerfile, README and traversal attempts all return 404, and there are no directory listings or stack traces. The only extra endpoint is a harmless /healthz.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: Server-side validation enforces type and length checks, malformed JSON gets a 400, bodies over 16 KB get a 413, and the client renders messages with textContent, so there's no XSS. The public contact endpoint has no rate limiting, and it logs submitter email addresses.

findings.title: Commercial site depends on an unclaimed free starter grant that runs out in about 9 hours
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: key creation returns "balance": 0.1, "creditsPerHour": 0.010733. process/deployment.json human_steps: 'covers about 9 hours of awake time ... After that, requests get HTTP 402/503 until credits are added' (blocking: false). process/context.json: use=commercial, balance_usd 0.0998.
findings.recommendation: Have the business claim the key, or deploy under a business-owned Cloudish account, and fund it with paid credits before relying on the site. Flag this as blocking for a production business site.

findings.title: Base image not pinned by digest
findings.recommendation: Pin the base image by digest (node:24-alpine@sha256:...) and update it on purpose.

findings.title: Deployed from an ad-hoc local tarball, not version-controlled source
findings.evidence: process/deploy.md: `tar --exclude='.env*' ... -czf /tmp/context.tar.gz .` POSTed to https://cloudish.ai/api/v1/projects; no git repo or commit recorded
findings.recommendation: Keep the source in an owner-controlled repository and deploy from a tagged commit so the deployed build can be traced.

findings.title: No Content-Security-Policy or frame-protection headers
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-14c8g-static-web.cloudish.app/ returns only content-type, x-content-type-options, cache-control and strict-transport-security; app/server.js:38 sets only X-Content-Type-Options
findings.recommendation: In send(), add `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `Referrer-Policy`.

findings.title: Contact endpoint has no rate limiting or bot protection
findings.evidence: app/server.js:46-77 handleContact accepts any number of valid POSTs; POST /api/contact with a valid body returned {"ok":true} 200
findings.recommendation: Add a simple per-IP rate limit or a honeypot field to slow abuse, especially once submissions are emailed or stored.

findings.title: Submitter email addresses are written to container logs
findings.evidence: app/server.js:74 `console.log(`contact submission from ${body.email.trim()}`)`; deploy logs show 'contact submission from a@b.co'
findings.recommendation: Log only that a submission occurred, or redact the address, to keep personal data out of platform logs.

findings.title: Undocumented /healthz endpoint
findings.recommendation: This is harmless. Keep it if the platform uses it, or remove it otherwise.

security.summary: A dependency-free Node.js container built and deployed carefully: the API key never left .env and was excluded from the build context, the container runs as non-root, nothing beyond the site is exposed, and input validation is sound. The main weakness is that this commercial site runs on an unclaimed key with only the free 0.1-credit grant, so it will stop serving after about 9 hours of awake time until someone adds credits. Minor gaps are an unpinned base image, a tarball deploy with no version control, missing CSP and frame headers, and no rate limiting on the contact endpoint.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: Static HTML/CSS plus a vanilla-JS fetch form and a small built-in http handler cover every requirement, including extensionless paths, 404s and JSON validation, without storage the task doesn't need.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: One ~130-line server file with zero dependencies and a four-line Dockerfile is about as small as a same-origin static site plus one endpoint can be.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: Cloudish only offers containers, so one small node:24-alpine container with scale-to-zero and wake-on-request is the platform's natural fit. The STACK.md reasoning matches the build, at the cost of cold starts after idle periods.

stack_fit.summary: A dependency-free Node.js http server in one small, sleeping container suits a three-page site with one JSON endpoint on a container-only platform. The STACK.md reasoning is sound and the build followed it.

light.basis: containers awake 10 h at their size's hourly rate; no bandwidth charges

busy.basis: containers awake 730 h at their size's hourly rate; no bandwidth charges

final_messages.build:
The Northwind Robotics site is built and works locally: the 7 automated tests pass, and I also checked every page and the contact endpoint against the Docker container with curl and in a real browser.

**Stack:** Cloudish only runs containers built from a Dockerfile, so I chose a single Node.js server with no dependencies. The three pages are plain HTML and CSS in `public/`, and `server.js` serves them and handles `POST /api/contact`. The `Dockerfile` uses the `node:24-alpine` image and listens on `$PORT` (default 8080). `STACK.md` compares this with Express or FastAPI, and with nginx plus a separate small backend.

**What I checked:**
- **Pages:** `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 with `text/html`. Each has a `<title>`, the viewport tag and navigation to the other pages.
- **404s:** unknown paths and `.html` versions like `/about.html` return 404.
- **Contact endpoint:** valid input returns 200 with `{"ok":true}`. A missing name, an invalid email or an empty message each return 400 with `{"ok":false,"error":"..."}`, and so does a body that isn't valid JSON.
- **Browser:** on a phone-sized screen, submitting the form called the API and showed a thank-you message without reloading the page. Screenshots at phone and desktop widths both looked right.

I also added a `/healthz` route that returns `ok`.

**To run it:**
- Locally: `npm start`, then open http://localhost:8080. There's nothing to install.
- Tests: `npm test`
- Container: `docker build -t northwind . && docker run -p 8080:8080 northwind`

I've stopped the server and container I started.
final_messages.deploy:
The site is live at **https://adb-14c8g-static-web.cloudish.app**, and every requirement in `TASK.md` passed when I tested it through that public URL.

**What I deployed:**
- **Cloudish key:** I created an API key named `adb-14c8g-static` myself; no signup was needed. It's saved only in `.env`, which is gitignored and was left out of the upload.
- **App:** a project called `adb-14c8g-static-web`. Cloudish built the container from the existing Dockerfile on its own servers.
- **Size:** the cheapest one, `shared`, at about $0.0107 per hour while it's running. It sleeps after 15 minutes without requests and costs nothing while asleep. The first request after a quiet spell takes a few extra seconds while it wakes up.
- **Cost:** I estimate about $1 a month at light traffic. If it never slept, the most it could cost is $7.84 a month.
- **Address:** I replaced the random subdomain Cloudish assigns with the memorable `adb-14c8g-static-web.cloudish.app`.

**What I tested on the public URL:**
- **Pages:** `/`, `/about` and `/contact` return 200 with HTML, and each has a title, the viewport tag and navigation.
- **404s:** unknown paths, and `.html` versions like `/about.html`, return 404.
- **Contact endpoint:** valid input returns 200 with `{"ok":true}`. A missing name, a bad email or an empty message each return 400 with an error message.
- **Browser:** filling in and submitting the form in a headless browser showed the confirmation without reloading the page.
- **Logs:** the container logs show the server started and received the test submissions.

**One step for a person (not urgent):** the new key only has Cloudish's free 0.1-credit starting balance. That covers about 9 hours of the site being awake, after which visitors get an error page until credits are added. To keep it running, someone needs to claim the key and add credits; how is listed under `human_steps` in `deployment.json`. Everything works now without it.

deployment_manifest.notes: Single dependency-free Node.js 24 container. It serves the static pages and POST /api/contact on the same origin. Cheapest size ('shared') with sleepAfterMinutes=15: it costs nothing while idle, and the first request after idle wakes it in a few seconds (cold start). Monthly cost depends on traffic: about $0 to $1 for light traffic, $7.84 maximum if it were awake all month. Every requirement was verified through the public HTTPS URL: /, /about and /contact return 200 text/html with title, viewport and nav; unknown paths and /about.html return 404; POST /api/contact returns 200 {ok:true} and 400 {ok:false,error} for a missing name, invalid email or empty message; a headless-browser submission of the /contact form showed the confirmation without a page reload. The API key is stored only in .env (gitignored and excluded from the build context). Redeploy: tar the directory (excluding .env*) and POST it to https://cloudish.ai/api/v1/projects with name=adb-14c8g-static-web.
